- **`README.md`** — summary of dataset, method, and findings

**Dataset:** DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsáki 2016), CA1 silicon-probe recordings from 4 rats running a novel 1.6 m linear track for reward.

**Key finding:** 50–70% of putative excitatory CA1 units across all 4 sessions showed statistically significant spatial tuning (circular-shift shuffle test on Skaggs spatial information), and their place fields collectively tiled the entire track — the canonical place-cell signature — reproducibly across four independent animals.

Two noteworthy things surfaced during the analysis, both handled and documented in the notebook:
1. The position `SpatialSeries.rate` field in this dataset is mislabeled — it actually stores the sampling *period* (~39 Hz), not a frequency. Used literally, it stretches 90k position samples across ~41 days instead of the true 40-minute session. I caught this by cross-checking against the epoch durations and physical track length.
2. The dataset's own linearized-position channel was valid on only ~7% of samples, so I derived a continuous linear position via PCA projection of the raw 2D tracking, validated against the sparse official channel (r = -1.000, i.e. perfectly correlated up to direction).
